stem:
Choose the best topic sentence to fill the blank.

__________. Employees must log in by 8:00 a.m. using the biometric scanner. Those who arrive after 8:15 a.m. are marked late. Three late marks in one month lead to a written warning.
choices: The office has strict rules about being on time.
Government offices use many kinds of modern machines.
Employees who are often late may receive a warning.
Workers should eat breakfast before coming to work.
answer: The office has strict rules about being on time.
hints: A good topic sentence covers every detail. Watch out for choices that are too broad or too narrow.
List the details: the log-in time, the time when you are marked late, and the warning. What do they have in common?
Test each choice: does it cover all three details? Reject a choice that fits only one detail, and one so broad that it could fit a very different paragraph.

solution.methodName: Find the sentence that covers all the others

steps.action: List the details: log in by 8:00 a.m., marked late after 8:15 a.m., a warning after three late marks.
steps.why: All three are rules about arriving on time.

steps.action: State the shared idea: the office has rules about coming to work on time.
Reject the choice that is too narrow.
steps.why: The choice about a warning covers only the last detail. It leaves out the log-in rule and the late mark.

steps.action: Reject the choices that are too broad or off the topic.
steps.why: The details are not about modern machines or breakfast.

steps.action: The best topic sentence is "The office has strict rules about being on time."

trapNotes.Government offices use many kinds of mod: It picks up the biometric scanner, but it is far too broad. The paragraph is about rules on time, not about machines.
trapNotes.Employees who are often late may receive: This is too narrow. It covers only the last detail and leaves out the log-in rule and the late mark.
trapNotes.Workers should eat breakfast before comi: Nothing in the paragraph mentions food. It may seem connected to mornings, but it is off the topic.
